topic.title: SIP money hit a record in a falling month: why steady investors don't hit pause

title: Record SIP money in a falling month: why a SIP suits a dip
description: Indians put a record Rs 32,490 crore into SIPs in September, a month when markets fell. Why a SIP is built for exactly that, worked out by code. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions. Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Comment if your SIP kept going

lines.text: Markets are falling. Time to stop my SIP, right?
Look at the data. In September, Indians put a record ₹32,490 Cr into SIPs.
Because a SIP is built for falls. The same amount buys more units when prices are low.
Take ₹5,000 a month for 15 years. You put in ₹9.0 L.
At an assumed 12% a year, it could grow to ₹25.2 L. But only if the payments keep coming.
I have seen many falls. The habit lasts longer than the fear.
Falls feel scary. But for a monthly investor, they also mean cheaper units.
